verses.text: Yahweh visited Sarah just as he had said, and did for her what he had promised.
Sarah became pregnant and gave Abraham a son in his old age, at the exact time God had told him.
Abraham named the son Sarah bore him Isaac.
Abraham circumcised Isaac when he was eight days old, just as God had commanded him.
Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac was born.
Sarah said, "God has given me laughter. Everyone who hears about this will laugh with me."
She said, "Who would have told Abraham that Sarah would nurse children? Yet I've given him a son in his old age."
The child grew and was weaned. Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.
Sarah saw Hagar the Egyptian's son, whom she had borne to Abraham, mocking.
So she said to Abraham, "Send this slave woman and her son away. The slave woman's son must not inherit along with my son Isaac."
This upset Abraham deeply because of his son.
But God said to Abraham, "Don't be upset about the boy or your servant. Listen to Sarah in everything she tells you, because your family line will be traced through Isaac.
I'll also make the son of the servant into a nation, because he is your child."

Abraham got up early, took bread and a container of water, and gave them to Hagar, placing them on her shoulder. Then he gave her the child and sent her away. She wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba.
When the water was gone, she placed the child under one of the bushes.
Then she went and sat down some distance away, about as far as an arrow can fly. She said, "I can't watch my child die." She sat there, raised her voice, and wept.
God heard the boy crying. The angel of God called to Hagar from the sky: "What's wrong, Hagar? Don't be afraid. God has heard the boy crying where he is.
Get up, pick up the boy, and hold him close. I'll make him into a great nation."
Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She went to it, filled the container, and gave the boy a drink.
God stayed with the boy as he grew up. He lived in the wilderness and became a skilled archer.
He lived in the wilderness of Paran. His mother found him a wife from the land of Egypt.
At that time Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, said to Abraham, "God is with you in everything you do.
So swear to me here before God that you won't deal falsely with me, my children, or my descendants. Show me and this land where you've lived as a foreigner the same kindness I've shown you."
Abraham answered, "I swear it."
Then Abraham complained to Abimelech about a well of water that Abimelech's servants had seized by force.
Abimelech said, "I don't know who did this. You never told me, and this is the first I've heard about it."
Abraham gave Abimelech sheep and cattle, and the two of them made a treaty.
Abraham set seven female lambs from the flock apart by themselves.
Abimelech asked Abraham, "What do these seven female lambs you've set apart mean?"
Abraham answered, "Accept these seven lambs from me as proof that I dug this well."
That's why the place was called Beersheba, because the two of them swore an oath there.
After making the treaty at Beersheba, Abimelech and Phicol, the commander of his army, returned to the land of the Philistines.
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba. There he called on Yahweh, the Everlasting God.
Abraham lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for a long time.
